title: SC junks petitions challenging ex-President Duterte's arrest

blocks.text: The Supreme Court (SC) has dismissed consolidated habeas corpus petitions challenging the arrest of former President Rodrigo Duterte, ruling that they have become moot and that Philippine courts cannot enforce the writ because he is already in the custody of another state.
In a press release issued Tuesday, the SC En Banc denied the consolidated petitions filed by Duterte’s children, Sebastian, Veronica and Paolo Duterte.
A day after Duterte’s arrest in March 2025, his children separately filed petitions for habeas corpus, a legal remedy used to challenge unlawful detention and seek a person’s release.

“The Office of the Solicitor General (OSG) argued that the petitions had become moot, or no longer needed to be resolved, because a writ of habeas corpus issued by Philippine courts cannot be enforced outside the country,” the SC said in its press release.
“It also maintained that the arrest complied with the Philippines’ international obligations,” it added.— MCG, GMA News
